about: Scripture events, batch 2: the prophets of the divided kingdom and the exile (DESIGN.md section 3). Fields work as in batch-1.json. Isaiah 36–39 and Jeremiah 39 and 52 are linked by batch 1, so they are not linked again here.
era: The prophets of the divided kingdom and the exile

events.title: Isaiah calls Judah to repent
events.summary: Isaiah sees a vision about Judah and Jerusalem. The people have turned away from the LORD. Their land is burned, and strangers eat their fields. God says he is weary of their offerings and feasts. He tells them to wash, stop doing evil, and seek justice. Their sins may become white as snow.

events.title: The mountain of the LORD's house in the last days
events.summary: Isaiah sees the LORD's house raised above the hills in the last days. Many nations go up to learn his ways. They beat their swords into plowshares. The proud will be brought low, and idols will be thrown away. Jerusalem's leaders and proud daughters face judgment. Afterward the LORD cleans Zion and covers it with cloud and fire.

alsoRead.note: Nephi copies Isaiah's words about the mountain of the LORD.
Micah gives the same promise.

events.title: Isaiah's song of the vineyard
events.summary: Isaiah sings of a friend who plants a fine vineyard. He does everything for it, but it grows only wild grapes. So he will tear down its wall and let it be trampled. The vineyard is Israel, and the vines are the people of Judah. Woes follow for greed, drunkenness, and calling evil good. God will raise a banner and call a swift army from far away.

events.title: Isaiah sees the Lord and is called
events.summary: In the year King Uzziah dies, Isaiah sees the Lord on a high throne. Seraphim cry that the LORD of Armies is holy. Isaiah fears, for he has unclean lips. A seraph touches his mouth with a burning coal. The Lord asks whom he should send, and Isaiah offers himself. He is told the people will hear but not understand.

alsoRead.note: Nephi copies Isaiah's call.

events.title: Isaiah gives Ahaz the sign of Immanuel
events.summary: Syria and Israel march against Jerusalem, and King Ahaz is afraid. Isaiah meets him and tells him not to fear these two kings. The LORD offers Ahaz a sign, and Ahaz refuses to ask. Isaiah says a virgin will bear a son named Immanuel. Before the child is grown, both enemy lands will be empty. Isaiah's own son is named for the coming plunder by Assyria.

alsoRead.note: Matthew applies the sign to the birth of Jesus.
Nephi copies the sign of Immanuel.

events.title: A child is born, and Assyria is the rod of God's anger
events.summary: People in Galilee who walked in darkness see a great light. A child is born who will rule on David's throne. His peace and government will have no end. The LORD's hand is still stretched out against proud Israel. God calls Assyria the rod of his anger. When Assyria boasts, God will burn it like thorns and save a remnant.

alsoRead.note: Matthew applies the great light to Jesus in Galilee.
Nephi copies the promise of the child.

events.title: A rod comes from the stem of Jesse
events.summary: A shoot grows from the stump of Jesse. The LORD's Spirit rests on him, and he judges the poor with fairness. The wolf lives with the lamb, and a little child leads them. The LORD raises a banner for the nations. He gathers the scattered people of Israel and Judah. The people sing praise, for God is their salvation.

alsoRead.note: The Lord explains who the stem of Jesse is.
Nephi copies this chapter.

events.title: Isaiah foretells Babylon's fall
events.summary: The LORD gathers an army from far lands against Babylon. The day of the LORD comes with cruel anger. The Medes will overthrow Babylon, and wild animals will live in its ruins. Israel will return to its land and taunt Babylon's king. The proud star of the morning has fallen from heaven. Messages against Assyria and Philistia close the chapter.

alsoRead.note: Nephi copies the fall of Lucifer.

events.title: Isaiah weeps for Moab
events.summary: Two Moabite cities fall in one night. Moab's people shave their heads and weep on the rooftops. Isaiah's own heart cries out for Moab. Moab is told to shelter Judah's refugees. A throne will be set up in mercy in David's tent. Within three years, Moab's glory will be brought low.

events.title: Messages to Damascus, Ethiopia, and Egypt
events.summary: Damascus will become a heap of ruins, and Ephraim will lose its strength. Ethiopia sends messengers in papyrus boats, and later brings gifts to Zion. The LORD rides a swift cloud to Egypt, and its idols tremble. Egyptians fight each other, and the Nile dries up. In that day Egypt and Assyria will worship with Israel. All three will be a blessing in the earth.

events.title: Isaiah walks barefoot as a sign against Egypt
events.summary: Assyria's commander captures the Philistine city of Ashdod. The LORD tells Isaiah to take off his sackcloth and sandals. Isaiah walks stripped and barefoot for three years. This is a sign against Egypt and Ethiopia. Assyria will lead their captives away the same way. Those who trusted in Egypt will be ashamed.

events.title: Isaiah sees Babylon and Tyre fall
events.summary: Isaiah sees a hard vision and shakes with pain. A watchman sees riders come and cries that Babylon has fallen. Its idols lie broken on the ground. Short messages for Edom and Arabia follow. Ships of Tarshish are told to howl, for Tyre's harbor is destroyed. After seventy years Tyre will trade again, and its gain will go to the LORD.

events.title: Jerusalem feasts, and Eliakim receives the key of David
events.summary: Jerusalem shouts on its rooftops while an enemy gathers. The people store water and tear down houses to strengthen the wall. They do not look to the God who made it. They say, let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die. The steward Shebna will be thrown out of his office. Eliakim will receive the key of David's house.

events.title: The earth is judged and death is swallowed up
events.summary: The LORD empties the earth, for its people have broken the everlasting covenant. The earth reels like a drunken man. The LORD reigns on Mount Zion. He makes a feast for all peoples and swallows up death forever. He wipes away tears from every face. The dead will live, and Israel will be gathered one by one.

events.title: Woe to Ephraim, and a cornerstone laid in Zion
events.summary: Isaiah cries woe to the proud crown of Ephraim's drunkards. Samaria will be eaten like the first ripe fig. Priests and prophets reel with wine. God teaches line upon line, precept upon precept. Jerusalem's rulers think they have a covenant with death. God lays a tested cornerstone in Zion, and their covenant will not stand.

events.title: A sealed book and a marvelous work
events.summary: Ariel, the city where David lived, will be besieged and brought low. She will speak low out of the dust. The people's vision is like a sealed book that no one can read. They honor God with their lips, but their hearts are far away. So God will do a marvelous work and a wonder. The deaf will hear the words of the book.

alsoRead.note: Nephi tells of the book in the last days.

events.title: Isaiah warns Judah not to trust Egypt
events.summary: Judah's leaders send envoys to Egypt for help against Assyria. Isaiah says Egypt's help is worthless and will bring shame. The people tell their prophets to speak only smooth things. God says their strength is in returning, rest, and quiet trust. The LORD waits to be gracious to them. He himself will defend Jerusalem, and Assyria will fall.

events.title: A king will reign in righteousness
events.summary: A king will reign in righteousness, and princes will rule with justice. Women at ease are warned that the palace will be deserted. Then the Spirit is poured out, and the desert becomes a fruitful field. Woe comes to the destroyer who has not been destroyed. The LORD is judge, lawgiver, and king. No one in Zion will say they are sick.

events.title: Edom is judged and the desert blossoms
events.summary: The LORD is angry with the nations and their armies. The sky rolls up like a scroll. His sword falls on Edom, and its land becomes a waste. Then the desert will rejoice and blossom like a rose. The blind will see, the deaf will hear, and the lame will leap. The redeemed will walk a highway of holiness to Zion.

events.title: Comfort my people: a voice in the wilderness
events.summary: God tells his prophet to comfort Jerusalem, for her hard service is over. A voice calls to prepare the LORD's way in the wilderness. All people are like grass, but God's word stands forever. He feeds his flock like a shepherd. No idol can compare with the Creator of the earth. Those who wait on the LORD will renew their strength.

alsoRead.note: Matthew applies the voice in the wilderness to John the Baptist.

events.title: The LORD's servant, and Israel his witness
events.summary: The LORD calls the nations to court and mocks their idols. He tells Israel not to fear, for he has chosen them. He presents his servant, who brings justice to the nations. The servant will be a light to the Gentiles. Israel is the LORD's witness that he alone is God. A man carves a god from the same log that warms his fire.

events.title: Cyrus is named, and Babylon's idols fall
events.summary: The LORD calls Cyrus his anointed and goes before him. He will open gates and give Cyrus hidden treasures. Cyrus will rebuild Jerusalem and free the exiles. Babylon's gods Bel and Nebo are carried off on tired animals. Babylon, the proud queen, will sit in the dust. Her magic and her stargazers cannot save her.

events.title: Israel is called out of Babylon and not forgotten
events.summary: The LORD has refined Israel in the furnace of affliction. He tells them to go out of Babylon with singing. The servant was called from the womb to bring Jacob back. He will also be a light to the Gentiles. Zion says the LORD has forgotten her. He answers that her walls are engraved on his palms. Kings will carry her children home.

alsoRead.note: Nephi reads this chapter to his brothers.
Nephi continues with the next chapter.

events.title: Awake, O Zion: beautiful feet on the mountains
events.summary: The servant gives his back to those who strike him. He does not turn away. The LORD tells Zion to look to Abraham, the rock it was cut from. Zion is told to wake, put on strength, and shake off the dust. The feet of the one who brings good news are beautiful. The LORD will bare his holy arm before all nations.

alsoRead.note: Jacob reads Isaiah's call for Zion to awake.
Abinadi explains the beautiful feet.
Jesus quotes these words to the Nephites.

events.title: The servant who bears our griefs
events.summary: The servant grows up like a root out of dry ground. He is despised and rejected, a man of sorrows. He carries the griefs and sorrows of others. He is wounded for their sins, and by his stripes they are healed. He is led like a lamb to the slaughter. He bears the sin of many and prays for the rebels.

alsoRead.note: Abinadi quotes this chapter to King Noah's priests.
Philip teaches an Ethiopian from this chapter.

events.title: Enlarge your tent, and come to the waters
events.summary: The barren woman is told to sing and enlarge her tent. The LORD left her for a moment but takes her back with mercy. His kindness will not leave her, though the mountains move. Everyone who thirsts is invited to come and buy without money. God's thoughts and ways are higher than ours. His word will not return to him empty.

alsoRead.note: Jesus quotes the enlarged tent to the Nephites.

events.title: Keep the Sabbath and the true fast
events.summary: Foreigners who keep the Sabbath will have a place in God's house. It will be called a house of prayer for all peoples. Israel's watchmen are blind, and idols are worshiped under green trees. The people fast but still quarrel and oppress their workers. The true fast frees the oppressed and feeds the hungry. Their sins have separated them from God.

events.title: Zion arises, and the Spirit anoints a messenger
events.summary: Zion is told to arise and shine, for her light has come. Nations come to her light, bringing her sons and daughters home. The LORD's Spirit anoints a messenger to bring good news to the meek. He will bind up the brokenhearted and free the captives. He gives beauty for ashes. Zion will have a new name.

alsoRead.note: Jesus reads this passage in the synagogue at Nazareth.

events.title: The LORD in red, and new heavens and a new earth
events.summary: One comes from Edom in red garments, for he has trodden the winepress alone. The people pray for God to tear open the heavens and come down. They are the clay, and he is the potter. God promises new heavens and a new earth. The wolf and the lamb will feed together. All flesh will come to worship before him.

alsoRead.note: The Lord will come in red at his Second Coming.

events.title: Jeremiah is called as a prophet
events.summary: Jeremiah is a priest's son from Anathoth in the days of King Josiah. God says he knew Jeremiah before he was born. Jeremiah says he is only a child. The LORD touches his mouth and puts his words there. He sees an almond branch and a boiling pot facing north. Disaster will come from the north.

events.title: Judah forsakes the fountain of living waters
events.summary: The LORD remembers how Israel once followed him in the wilderness. Now they have left him, the fountain of living waters. They dug broken cisterns that hold no water. Judah has been unfaithful like a wife who leaves her husband. Judah saw Israel sent away, yet did not turn back. God still calls them to return, and he will give them shepherds.

events.title: Jeremiah warns of disaster from the north
events.summary: A trumpet warns of a lion coming from the north. Jeremiah feels anguish as he hears the alarm of war. God tells him to search Jerusalem for one person who does justice. Rich and poor alike refuse to turn back. Prophets and priests cry peace when there is no peace. The people will not walk in the old paths.

events.title: Jeremiah's temple sermon, and his trial
events.summary: Early in Jehoiakim's reign, Jeremiah stands at the temple gate. They steal and worship Baal, yet trust in the temple to save them. God's house has become a den of robbers. It will be ruined like Shiloh. Priests and prophets say Jeremiah must die. Elders recall that Micah said the same, and Ahikam protects him.

events.title: Jeremiah weeps for his people
events.summary: Even the stork knows its season, but the people do not know God's law. Jeremiah asks if there is no balm in Gilead. He wishes his head were a spring of tears. No one can trust a neighbor or a brother. Idols cannot speak and must be carried. The LORD is the true God, the living God, and everlasting King.

events.title: The covenant is broken, and Anathoth plots against Jeremiah
events.summary: The LORD tells Jeremiah to proclaim the words of the covenant. The fathers did not obey it, and their children have turned to other gods. Judah has as many gods as it has towns. God tells Jeremiah not to pray for them. Men of Anathoth plot to kill him. Jeremiah was like a gentle lamb led to the slaughter.

events.title: Jeremiah's ruined linen belt
events.summary: The LORD tells Jeremiah to buy a linen belt and wear it. Then he hides it in a rock by the Euphrates. Many days later he digs it up, and it is ruined. God says he will ruin the pride of Judah the same way. Israel once clung to him like a belt. Jars full of wine stand for a people filled with drunkenness.

events.title: Drought, and Jeremiah's complaint
events.summary: A drought strikes Judah, and the cisterns are empty. Jeremiah pleads for the people. The LORD says false prophets promise peace he never sent. Even Moses and Samuel could not turn his heart toward this people. Jeremiah grieves that everyone curses him. God's words were his joy, and God promises to make him a bronze wall.

events.title: The tree planted by the waters
events.summary: Judah's sin is written on its heart with an iron pen. Whoever trusts in man is like a shrub in the desert. Whoever trusts the LORD is like a tree planted by water. The heart is deceitful above all things. Jeremiah asks God to heal him. The people must keep the Sabbath and carry no loads through the gates.

events.title: The potter's clay and the broken jar
events.summary: The LORD sends Jeremiah to watch a potter at his wheel. The pot is spoiled, and the potter makes it again. Israel is like clay in God's hands. Later Jeremiah takes elders to the valley of Hinnom with a clay jar. He breaks it before them. God will break the city the same way.

events.title: Pashhur puts Jeremiah in the stocks
events.summary: Pashhur, a chief officer of the temple, hears Jeremiah's words. He has Jeremiah beaten and put in the stocks. The next day Jeremiah says Pashhur will go captive to Babylon. Jeremiah complains that he has become a laughingstock. He tries to stop speaking God's word. It burns in his bones like fire, and he cannot hold it in.

events.title: Jeremiah warns the kings of Judah
events.summary: King Zedekiah asks Jeremiah if the LORD will save the city from Babylon. Jeremiah says God himself will fight against Jerusalem. Those who surrender to Babylon will live. The king must do justice and protect the orphan and widow. Shallum will die in exile. Jehoiakim will be buried like a donkey. Coniah will have no heir on the throne.

events.title: A righteous Branch for David, and false prophets
events.summary: The LORD condemns the shepherds who scatter his flock. He will gather the remnant and give them good shepherds. He will raise a righteous Branch for David. That king will be called the LORD our Righteousness. God rebukes prophets who tell their own dreams. His word is like fire and like a hammer that breaks rock.

events.title: Two baskets of figs
events.summary: Nebuchadnezzar has carried King Jeconiah and Judah's craftsmen to Babylon. The LORD shows Jeremiah two baskets of figs before the temple. One basket holds good figs, and the other bad. The good figs are the exiles, whom God will bring back. He will give them a heart to know him. The bad figs are Zedekiah and those who stay.

events.title: Seventy years under Babylon, and the cup of wrath
events.summary: In Jehoiakim's fourth year, Jeremiah speaks to all Judah. For twenty-three years he has warned them, and they have not listened. So Nebuchadnezzar will come against the land. The nations will serve Babylon for seventy years. Then Babylon itself will be punished. The nations must drink the cup of the LORD's anger.

events.title: Jeremiah's yoke and Hananiah's false prophecy
events.summary: The LORD tells Jeremiah to wear a yoke on his neck. Judah and its neighbors must serve the king of Babylon to live. The prophet Hananiah says God has broken Babylon's yoke. He breaks Jeremiah's yoke in the temple. Jeremiah says God will put an iron yoke in its place. Hananiah dies that same year.

events.title: Jeremiah's letter to the exiles in Babylon
events.summary: Jeremiah sends a letter from Jerusalem to the exiles in Babylon. They should build houses, plant gardens, and raise families. They must seek the peace of the city where they live. After seventy years God will bring them home. He has plans to give them hope. False prophets among the exiles will be punished.

events.title: God promises a new covenant
events.summary: The LORD tells Jeremiah to write his words in a book. He will bring Israel and Judah back to their land. He has loved Israel with an everlasting love. Rachel weeps for her children in Ramah, but they will return. God will make a new covenant with Israel and Judah. He will write his law on their hearts.

alsoRead.note: Hebrews quotes the promise of a new covenant.
Matthew recalls Rachel weeping in Ramah.

events.title: Jeremiah buys a field at Anathoth
events.summary: Babylon besieges Jerusalem, and Jeremiah is held in the court of the guard. His cousin Hanamel asks him to buy a field in Anathoth. Jeremiah pays the silver and has Baruch store the deed in a clay jar. It is a sign that fields will be bought again in this land. Nothing is too hard for the LORD. A Branch will rise for David.

events.title: Judah frees its slaves, then takes them back
events.summary: Babylon's army attacks Jerusalem and Judah's last towns. Jeremiah tells Zedekiah the city will fall and he will see Babylon's king. The people make a covenant to free their Hebrew slaves. Then they take the slaves back. So God gives them freedom of another kind, to the sword and famine.

events.title: The faithful Rechabites
events.summary: In Jehoiakim's days, Jeremiah brings the Rechabite family into a temple room. He sets wine before them. They refuse, for their ancestor Jonadab told them never to drink it. They have kept his command for generations. Judah has not kept God's words. So the Rechabites are blessed, and Judah will be punished.

events.title: Jehoiakim burns Jeremiah's scroll
events.summary: In Jehoiakim's fourth year, the LORD tells Jeremiah to write his words on a scroll. Baruch writes as Jeremiah speaks. Baruch reads the scroll in the temple, and the officials take it to the king. Jehoiakim cuts it apart and burns it in his fire. Jeremiah and Baruch hide. Jeremiah dictates the words again, with more added.

events.title: Jeremiah is imprisoned and lowered into a cistern
events.summary: Egypt's army marches out, and Babylon pulls back from Jerusalem. Jeremiah says Babylon will return and burn the city. He is arrested as a deserter and put in a dungeon. Officials have him lowered into a muddy cistern to die. Ebed-melech the Ethiopian pulls him out with ropes. Zedekiah meets him in secret but will not surrender.

events.title: Gedaliah is murdered at Mizpah
events.summary: Babylon's captain frees Jeremiah from his chains at Ramah. Jeremiah chooses to stay with Gedaliah, the new governor at Mizpah. Scattered Jews return and gather the harvest. Johanan warns Gedaliah of a plot, but he does not believe it. Ishmael of the royal family kills Gedaliah at a meal. Johanan rescues the captives Ishmael took.

events.title: The remnant of Judah flees to Egypt
events.summary: The people ask Jeremiah to pray for guidance and promise to obey. The LORD says to stay in Judah and not go to Egypt. The leaders call Jeremiah a liar. They take everyone to Tahpanhes in Egypt, with Jeremiah and Baruch. Jeremiah hides stones there for Nebuchadnezzar's throne. The Jews in Egypt keep burning incense to the queen of heaven.

events.title: Babylon defeats Egypt at Carchemish
events.summary: Jeremiah's messages to the nations begin with Egypt. Pharaoh Necho's army is defeated by Nebuchadnezzar at Carchemish. Egypt rose like the Nile, but its soldiers flee in terror. Babylon will come and strike Egypt's own land. Jacob is told not to fear, for God will save him from far away.

events.title: Jeremiah's messages to Judah's neighbors
events.summary: A flood from the north rises over the Philistines. Moab's towns fall one by one, and its god Chemosh goes into exile. Ammon trusted in its treasures and will be ruined. Edom lives in the rocks, but God will bring it down. Damascus, Kedar, and Elam will also fall. God promises to restore Moab, Ammon, and Elam in later days.

events.title: Jeremiah foretells the fall of Babylon
events.summary: A nation from the north will attack Babylon, and its gods will be shamed. Israel and Judah will come weeping and seek the way to Zion. Babylon was a golden cup that made the earth drunk. Now it falls suddenly. Jeremiah writes these words on a scroll for Seraiah to take to Babylon. Seraiah reads it, ties a stone to it, and throws it into the Euphrates.

events.title: Jerusalem is mourned in Lamentations
events.summary: Five poems mourn Jerusalem after Babylon destroys it. The city sits alone like a widow, and no one comforts her. The Lord has thrown down her walls and his own sanctuary. Children faint from hunger in the streets. One man still hopes, for the LORD's mercies are new every morning. The people ask God to remember them and restore them.

events.title: Ezekiel acts out the siege of Jerusalem
events.summary: Ezekiel is among the exiles in Babylon. God tells him to draw Jerusalem on a brick and set a siege around it. He lies on his side for many days to bear the people's guilt. He eats rationed bread to show coming famine. He shaves his hair and divides it into three parts. A third will die by plague and famine, a third by sword. The rest are scattered.

events.title: The end has come on the land
events.summary: Ezekiel speaks against the mountains of Israel. A sword will fall on the hilltop shrines, and the altars will be ruined. A remnant will remember the LORD in exile. The end has come on the four corners of the land. Silver and gold cannot save the people. They will seek a vision from the prophet in vain.

events.title: Ezekiel sees the glory leave the temple
events.summary: Ezekiel sits with Judah's elders in his house in Babylon. In a vision he is carried to the temple in Jerusalem. He sees idols, women weeping for Tammuz, and men bowing to the sun. A man in linen marks those who mourn the city's sins. The glory of God rises from the temple and leaves the city. God promises the exiles a new heart and a new spirit.

events.title: Ezekiel packs his bags for exile
events.summary: God tells Ezekiel to pack bags for exile while the people watch. In the evening he digs through the wall and carries his bag out. He covers his face so he cannot see the land. This is a sign that Jerusalem's prince and people will go into captivity. The people say visions fail. God says his word will not be delayed any longer.

events.title: Ezekiel condemns false prophets and idols of the heart
events.summary: God speaks against prophets who follow their own spirit. They cry peace when there is no peace. They cover a weak wall with whitewash, and it will fall. Elders come to Ezekiel with idols in their hearts. God says even Noah, Daniel, and Job could save only themselves. A remnant will still survive.

events.title: Parables of the vine, the unfaithful bride, and the eagles
events.summary: Jerusalem is like vine wood, good only for the fire. God found her as an abandoned baby and later married her. She trusted in her beauty and was unfaithful with the nations. Still God will remember his covenant with her. A riddle tells of two eagles and a vine. Judah's king broke his oath to Babylon and turned to Egypt.

events.title: Each person answers for their own sins
events.summary: The people say the fathers ate sour grapes, and the children's teeth ache. God says they will not use this proverb any more. Each person will answer for their own sins. A righteous son will not die for a wicked father. If the wicked turn from their sins, they will live. God takes no pleasure in anyone's death.

events.title: Ezekiel recounts Israel's rebellion
events.summary: Ezekiel sings a lament for Israel's princes, who were caught like young lions. Elders come to ask of the LORD, but he will not answer them. He recounts their history from Egypt onward. God gave them his statutes and his Sabbaths. Again and again they rebelled. Still he will gather them and accept them on his holy mountain.

events.title: The sword of Babylon and the city of bloodshed
events.summary: God's sword is sharpened and drawn against Jerusalem. Babylon's king stands at a fork in the road and casts lots. The lot points to Jerusalem. The crown will be overturned until the rightful one comes. Jerusalem is a city of bloodshed that wrongs the orphan and widow. God looked for someone to stand in the gap and found no one.

events.title: The parable of two sisters
events.summary: God tells a story of two sisters, Oholah and Oholibah. Oholah is Samaria, and Oholibah is Jerusalem. Samaria chased after Assyria and was destroyed by it. Jerusalem saw this and became even worse. She chased after Assyria, Babylon, and Egypt. She will drink her sister's cup.

events.title: The siege begins, and Ezekiel's wife dies
events.summary: God tells Ezekiel to write down the day Babylon's siege of Jerusalem begins. He gives a parable of a rusted pot set on the fire. Then God tells Ezekiel his wife will die. Ezekiel must not mourn her openly. She dies that evening. So the people will not mourn when the temple falls.

events.title: Ammon, Moab, Edom, and Philistia are judged
events.summary: God speaks against four neighbors of Judah. Ammon clapped and rejoiced when the temple was profaned. Moab said Judah was like every other nation. Edom took revenge on Judah. The Philistines acted with old hatred. Each will know that God is the LORD.

events.title: Ezekiel foretells the fall of Tyre
events.summary: Tyre rejoiced when Jerusalem fell. God will bring many nations against it like waves. Nebuchadnezzar will besiege it, and it will become a bare rock. Ezekiel laments Tyre as a beautiful ship sunk at sea. Tyre's ruler says he is a god, but he is only a man. Sidon is judged too, and Israel will be gathered in safety.

events.title: Ezekiel speaks against Pharaoh and Egypt
events.summary: Pharaoh is a great monster lying in the Nile. He says the river is his own. God will put hooks in his jaws and leave him in the desert. Nebuchadnezzar will take Egypt as wages for his work against Tyre. Egypt is a tall cedar that will be cut down like Assyria. Ezekiel sings a lament as Pharaoh goes down to the pit.

events.title: Ezekiel the watchman hears that Jerusalem has fallen
events.summary: God makes Ezekiel a watchman for Israel. A watchman who does not warn the people shares their guilt. God takes no pleasure in the death of the wicked. A refugee arrives in Babylon and says the city has fallen. Then Ezekiel's mouth is opened. The people enjoy his words like a love song but do not obey them.

events.title: Ezekiel speaks against Mount Seir
events.summary: God tells Ezekiel to speak against Mount Seir, the land of Edom. Edom kept an old hatred and gave Israel to the sword. It wanted to take the land of Israel and Judah. God heard its boasting. Mount Seir will become a waste.

events.title: A river flows from the temple
events.summary: In his vision of a new temple, Ezekiel sees water flow from under the threshold. It grows from ankle-deep to a river too deep to cross. It heals the Dead Sea, and fish fill it. Trees on its banks bear fruit every month. The land is divided among the twelve tribes. The city's name will be The LORD Is There.

events.title: Daniel and his friends refuse the king's food
events.summary: Nebuchadnezzar takes Jerusalem and carries off temple vessels and young nobles. Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah are trained for the king's court. Daniel will not defile himself with the king's food and wine. They eat vegetables and drink water for ten days. They look healthier than the others. God gives them knowledge, and Daniel understands dreams.

events.title: Daniel tells Nebuchadnezzar's dream of the great image
events.summary: Nebuchadnezzar has a dream and orders his wise men to tell it. No one can, so he orders them all killed. Daniel and his friends pray, and God shows Daniel the dream. A great image has a gold head and feet of iron and clay. A stone cut without hands breaks it and fills the earth. God will set up a kingdom that never ends.

alsoRead.note: The stone cut without hands will fill the earth.

events.title: Three friends in the fiery furnace
events.summary: Nebuchadnezzar sets up a huge gold image and orders all to bow. Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego refuse. They say God can save them, but even if not, they will not bow. They are thrown bound into a furnace heated seven times hotter. The king sees four men walking free in the fire. They come out unharmed, and the king praises their God.

events.title: Nebuchadnezzar is humbled
events.summary: Nebuchadnezzar tells this story himself in a letter to all peoples. He dreams of a great tree that is cut down. Daniel says the tree is the king. A year later the king boasts about the Babylon he built. He is driven out and eats grass like an ox until seven times pass. When he looks to heaven, his mind and his kingdom return.

events.title: The writing on the wall at Belshazzar's feast
events.summary: King Belshazzar drinks from the gold cups taken from Jerusalem's temple. A hand appears and writes on the palace wall. No wise man can read it. Daniel says God has numbered the kingdom and ended it. The king has been weighed and found wanting. That night Belshazzar is killed, and Darius the Mede takes the kingdom.

events.title: Daniel in the lions' den
events.summary: King Darius sets Daniel over his officials. Jealous rivals persuade the king to ban prayer to anyone but him for thirty days. Daniel still prays three times a day toward Jerusalem. He is thrown into a den of lions. God sends an angel to shut the lions' mouths. Darius praises Daniel's God, and the rivals are thrown to the lions.

events.title: Daniel's prayer and the seventy weeks
events.summary: Daniel reads in Jeremiah that Jerusalem's ruin will last seventy years. He fasts and confesses the sins of his people. He asks God to forgive them and restore his city. Gabriel comes while Daniel is still praying. He says seventy weeks are set for the people and the holy city. An anointed one will come, and later be cut off.

events.title: Hosea's marriage and God's faithful love
events.summary: God speaks of Israel as a wife who chased other lovers. She does not know that God gave her grain, wine, and oil. He will take back his gifts and end her feasts. Then he will lead her into the wilderness and speak tenderly to her. He will break the bow and sword, so his people lie down safely. He will betroth her to himself forever.

events.title: Israel sows the wind and reaps the whirlwind
events.summary: Israel is like a cake not turned, and like a silly dove. It calls to Egypt and goes to Assyria. The people make kings and idols without God. They sow the wind and will reap the whirlwind. The calf of Bethel will be carried to Assyria. It is time to seek the LORD and break up the unplowed ground.

events.title: Out of Egypt I called my son
events.summary: God loved Israel as a child and called his son out of Egypt. He taught Ephraim to walk and led him with cords of love. His heart cannot give Israel up. Ephraim makes treaties with Assyria and Egypt and kisses calf idols. Israel will vanish like the morning mist. Yet God will ransom them from the grave.

alsoRead.note: Matthew applies these words to the child Jesus.

events.title: Joel foretells the day of the LORD and the outpoured Spirit
events.summary: A trumpet sounds in Zion, for the day of the LORD is near. An army advances like fire. God calls the people to return with all their heart. Afterward he will pour out his Spirit on all flesh. Sons and daughters will prophesy. God will gather the nations to the valley of decision.

alsoRead.note: Peter quotes Joel on the day of Pentecost.

events.title: Amos speaks against the nations and Israel
events.summary: Amos is a herdsman from Tekoa in the days of Jeroboam of Israel. The LORD roars from Zion. Amos names the sins of Damascus, Gaza, Tyre, Edom, Ammon, and Moab. Then he turns to Judah, which rejected the LORD's law. Last he turns to Israel. They sell the poor for a pair of sandals.

events.title: God reveals his secret to the prophets
events.summary: God chose Israel alone of all the families of the earth. So he will punish them for their sins. The Lord does nothing without revealing his secret to his prophets. The wealthy women of Samaria crush the poor. God sent famine, drought, and plague, yet Israel did not return. Israel must prepare to meet its God.

events.title: Seek the LORD and let justice roll down
events.summary: Amos sings a funeral song for Israel. God tells the people to seek him and live. They hate anyone who speaks the truth. God rejects their feasts and offerings. He wants justice to roll down like waters. Those at ease in Zion and Samaria lie on ivory beds. They will be the first to go into exile.

events.title: A famine of hearing the word, and David's tent restored
events.summary: God shows Amos a basket of summer fruit, for Israel's end has come. Merchants cheat the poor with false scales. A famine is coming, not of bread, but of hearing the LORD's words. Amos sees the Lord beside the altar, and no one escapes. Israel will be sifted among the nations. Then God will raise up David's fallen tent.

events.title: Obadiah speaks against Edom
events.summary: Obadiah's vision concerns Edom, the people descended from Esau. Edom lives high in the rocks and thinks no one can bring it down. God will bring it down even from among the stars. Edom stood aside and rejoiced when Jerusalem fell. As Edom has done, it will be done to Edom. Saviors will come up on Mount Zion.

events.title: Jonah flees and is swallowed by a fish
events.summary: The LORD tells Jonah to preach against Nineveh. Jonah boards a ship at Joppa going the other way. A violent storm threatens to break the ship. The sailors cast lots, and the lot falls on Jonah. They throw him into the sea, and the storm stops. A great fish swallows Jonah.

alsoRead.note: Jesus compares his burial to Jonah's three days in the fish.

events.title: Nineveh repents at Jonah's preaching
events.summary: The LORD calls Jonah a second time, and he goes to Nineveh. He says the city will be overthrown in forty days. The people believe God, and the king calls a fast. God sees them turn from evil and spares the city. Jonah is angry. God asks if he should not pity a great city full of people.

events.title: Micah warns Samaria and Jerusalem
events.summary: Micah of Moresheth speaks about Samaria and Jerusalem. The LORD comes down, and the mountains melt under him. Samaria will become a heap of rubble. Judah's rulers hate good and devour the people. Its prophets speak for money. So Zion will be plowed like a field.

alsoRead.note: Elders recall Micah's words at Jeremiah's trial.

events.title: Micah sees peace in Zion and a ruler from Bethlehem
events.summary: In the last days the mountain of the LORD's house will rise above the hills. Nations will beat their swords into plowshares. Each will sit under their own vine and fig tree. Jerusalem is besieged, and its ruler is struck on the cheek. A ruler will come from small Bethlehem. The remnant of Jacob will be like a lion among the nations.

alsoRead.note: The scribes tell Herod that the Christ will be born in Bethlehem.
Jesus quotes the lion among the nations.

events.title: What the LORD requires
events.summary: The LORD brings a case against his people, with the mountains as witnesses. He brought them out of Egypt. He does not want thousands of rams or rivers of oil. He asks them to do justice, love mercy, and walk humbly with God. Micah grieves that the faithful have vanished. He will wait for God, who delights in mercy.

events.title: Nahum foretells the fall of Nineveh
events.summary: Nahum's message is about Nineveh, the capital of Assyria. The LORD is slow to anger, but he will not leave the guilty unpunished. He is a stronghold for those who trust him. Chariots race through Nineveh's streets, and the river gates open. Woe to the city of blood, full of lies and plunder. All who hear of its fall will clap their hands.

events.title: Habakkuk waits for the vision: the just shall live by faith
events.summary: Habakkuk stands at his watch post to hear what God will say. The LORD tells him to write the vision plainly on tablets. It will surely come, though it waits. The righteous will live by faith. Woes follow for the greedy, the violent, and those who trust in idols. Though the fields fail, Habakkuk will rejoice in the LORD.

alsoRead.note: Paul quotes the just living by faith.

events.title: Zephaniah warns of the day of the LORD
events.summary: Zephaniah speaks in the days of King Josiah. The great day of the LORD is near, a day of wrath. The humble are told to seek righteousness and humility. Philistia, Moab, Ammon, Ethiopia, and Assyria will be judged. Jerusalem's leaders are like roaring lions. Yet God will gather a humble remnant and rejoice over them with singing.
